# Review - PR 611 @ f93f882b7f1e1b0f2bb1a2dc0cacabe632211094

Independent review by a Claude Opus helper (owner-authorized 2026-09-17); no author, fixer or prior reviewer context reused. Trusted prompt, persona and policy ref: `aa79e10c0c3ecfa0188b0a266a97815fcbb16a28`. Tooling-only change (one new 130-line Python helper, a 23-line block in the owner estimate script, a 110-line offline unit test); no Lean source, blueprint, doc, workflow or CI-gating file is touched.

## Findings

- [x] F1 (code; minor, non-blocking) results/telemetry/owner-tools/estimate.sh:79 - the digit guard `case "$LF$LC"` concatenates the two fields, so a non-empty `LF` with an empty `LC` passes it and `printf` then emits `"lean_code_lines":,` - an unparsable row in the append-only `estimates.jsonl`. Not reachable at this head (the helper prints three fields or exits non-zero, and the `--paths`/`--rev` paths are covered by the test), so it is a latent robustness gap, not a defect of this change; testing the two variables separately (`case "$LF" in ... ; case "$LC" in ...`) would close it. I reproduced all three branches in a throwaway sandbox: success gives `"lean_code_lines":76082,"lean_files":312` and the clause; helper failure gives `null,null` and drops the clause (both valid JSON); a truncated helper output gives the malformed row above.
- [x] F2 (code; minor, non-blocking) results/telemetry/owner-tools/lean-loc.py:41 - the counted scope is exactly `MIPStarRE/QPBT` plus `MIPStarRE/QPBT.lean`, so the shared modules the QPBT files import (`MIPStarRE/Quantum`, 12 files; `MIPStarRE/LDT`, imported by 37 QPBT files) are outside the figure. That is stated in the helper docstring but not in the posted clause or the PR body. It matches the label "QPBT Lean code" and, more importantly, it is the same pathspec the sorry-site count in the same sentence already uses (`estimate.sh` `count_at`), so the two numbers on the tracker line describe the same tree; no change requested.

## Review

Scope. Base is `main`; `git merge-base github/main f93f882b` = `137bf02d`, so the main-relative diff carries two commits, `6dbca3a6` (PR 606, the real-sorry-site rule) and `f93f882b` (this PR). I reviewed this PR's own commit in full and only smoke-tested 606's, which is under review in its own pull request: `python3 -m unittest scripts.tests.test_estimate_sorry_count` passes (4 tests). There are no earlier marked reviews of PR 611, so there was no prior finding to re-check.

Counting rule. The rule is stated in the helper docstring and in the `estimate.sh` comment block: blank lines and lines lying wholly inside a line, block, doc or module-doc comment are not code; code with a trailing comment is. The helper *imports* `local/bin/pr_merge.py` `lean_code_line_mask` (the merge-title Lean-delta rule) instead of re-implementing it, which is the right call under the no-duplicate-helper rule and keeps the two published figures from drifting. Non-project trees cannot leak in: `count_revision` lists names with `git ls-tree -r` at a revision, so only tracked files are seen and `.lake/packages` (untracked) can never be counted; the working tree is never read in `--rev` mode.

Reproduction. Independently recounted `github/main` from the branch, read-only, with my own implementation of the stated rule (a separate left-to-right scanner, not the project's): 312 files, 76082 code lines, 102072 total lines - identical to what the helper prints (`312 76082 102072`) and to the number in the PR body, and the raw total matches `git show ... | wc -l` = 102072. The count is over `github/main` at the time of this review.

Fail-safe and cost. `set -u` is on and there is no `set -e`; the helper call is guarded by `if`, stderr is discarded, the digit guard rejects junk, and `--format-clause` failure only drops the clause. `count_revision` raises on an empty listing, so the script prints no figure rather than a misleading `0`; the sandbox run above confirms the failure path posts the old sentence unchanged with `null` in both new JSON keys. Work is bounded by the tracked QPBT file list (312 `git show` calls): measured 2.24 s wall on ghz, against an `estimate.sh` run that already does one `gh pr view` plus a fetch per open PR, so the added cost is negligible - though the git subprocesses carry no timeout, like the rest of the script.

Wiring and tests. `estimate.sh` `cd`s to the repo root before use, so the relative helper path resolves; the clause is appended inside the existing `<sub>` detail line (updates stay one-liners) and the two new JSON keys are appended at the end of the record, leaving old rows and readers alone. `scripts/tests/test_estimate_lean_loc.py` (7 tests) passes here and is picked up by `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests` (`pr-ci.yml`) and by the pre-commit hook; it pins the counting rule on a fixture tree, the failure path, the clause wording including the singular "1 file", and that `estimate.sh` really carries the helper and both keys.

CI at the exact head: I read `repos/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/commits/f93f882b7f1e1b0f2bb1a2dc0cacabe632211094/status` myself - combined `success`, 9/9 contexts green (`local-ci/summary`, `build`, `blueprint-render`, `blueprint-sync`, `paper-gaps`, `file-length`, `proof-debt`, `proof-evasion`, `statement-origin`).

Not checked: deployment of the tool (out of scope by the request - the tracked copy is what I reviewed, the `/home/drx/bin` copy is not touched by this PR); the substance of PR 606; the behaviour of the helper on file names needing git path quoting (ASCII-only in this tree today; such a name would fail closed, dropping the clause). Proof integrity is vacuous here: no Lean file, statement, blueprint tag or audit is touched, and no `sorry`, `axiom` or `native_decide` appears in the diff.

Every docstring locator I opened (08:1426-1447, 14:1862-1876, 14:1864-1875) points at the passage it claims.
